verdict.justification: A provides the stronger, more defensible management report while matching the workbook's core totals, supplier shares, and resolution-time statistics. Its supplier scorecard and quantified recurring-theme analysis make it easier to connect incident volume, financial exposure, and recommended actions. Most importantly, A distinguishes confirmed warehouse-caused incidents from ESD packaging and water-damage cases whose responsible party is not established; B instead concludes that “12% of incidents are caused by our own handling” and directs supplier cost recovery without establishing responsibility. A also preserves missing costs as unknown through labels such as “Not recorded*,” whereas B explicitly treats blanks as zero and asserts that replacements explain the absence of costs. B's statement that Aperion's lost profit is “mentioned but not quantified” overlooks the four associated $1,000 resolution-cost entries, which A explicitly discusses. Although A is denser and would benefit from tighter slide editing, its more complete analysis and better treatment of uncertainty make it the preferable deliverable.
